x: Tom Scrimshaw, off 4 yards, our half-mile track International, tried a turn of sprinting, and very nearly caught Bennett off 10 yards, a proof that he is keeping himself fit during the close season.

Brodie made a good "come-back" in winning the short sprint off 7 yards; whilst Bennett, always improving, annexed the 220 yards handicap. White thanked the handicapper for his generosity, in winning the "half" from 30 yards in 1 min. 55 2-5 secs—excellent running.

Of the sprinters, Brodie and Kealey have been prominent, with Wiley coming along nicely, and others such as Basford and Stroud (until his leg "gave way") of the seniors, and Mewes, the Crillys, Bennett and others of the younger brigade, keeping up their average.
In the 4 x 220 yards we were fourth (Mewes, Bennett, Stower, Christie), a position we also filled in the 4 x 440 yards event (Jones, Stower, Clubb, Pack).

The 4 x 300 yards was in the nature of a tragedy for us; for with Stroud going first, and Bennett continuing the good work, we saw Michael having a neck and neck race with the Croydon man over the third stage.
In the Middlesex County Championships four sprinters—Botwright, Wiley, Pritchard and yours truly, Bennett—entered and all gained County Standards.
Unfortunately we were unable to turn out a very strong team, but the home team were given quite a good match. Bowers and Bennett finished 2nd and 5th in both 100 yds. and 220 yds.

The match against Southgate, at Broomfield Park, took place in glorious weather, and some keen racing was seen, as the result below will show, the club winning with 58 points to 51 points. 100 Yards.—(1) Marin (S); (2) Bowers (B); (5) Bennett (B). 10.5. 880 Yards.—(1) Marchant (B); (2) Orton (B). 2mins. 5.4.

It leaves me to say that I want to see the arrival of our 'young promises' such as Morris, Bennett, Maxwell, Dunsford, Robson, Miss Jane Pritchard, Miss Anna Matthews and Miss Diana Cook bursting onto the scene.
